findings.description: initRepo's `git init` now goes through runGit without GIT_ENV, so GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM are no longer /dev/null; init-time keys (init.templateDir copying template hooks into .git/hooks, init.defaultObjectFormat, init.defaultRefFormat) from /etc/gitconfig or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config leak into every test repo and stay there.
findings.body:
**Test repos lose their git-config isolation.** This file's own rule (L25-L27) says *"Test repos must not inherit the developer's global git config (hooks, signing)"*. The old call enforced it by passing `GIT_ENV`, which sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: '/dev/null'` and `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM: '/dev/null'`. The new call passes no env:

```ts
runGit(repo, ['init', '-b', 'main']);
```

Nothing in `runGit` takes over that job. It builds its env as `{ ...scrubbedGitEnv(), ...opts.env, ...GIT_HISTORY_ENV }` (`src/core/git-diff.client.ts:524`):
- `scrubbedGitEnv` (L29-36) only removes the `GIT_DIR` family and the `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS/COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n` keys.
- `GIT_HISTORY_ENV` only sets the replace/graft keys.
- `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` pins `core.hooksPath` and the signing keys, but no `init.*` key and no `--template=`.

The production `git init` that goes through `runGit` passes `--template=` explicitly for this reason (`src/core/merge-gate.service.ts:2826`).

The callers' `beforeEach` stubs `HOME` to a temp dir, so `~/.gitconfig` stays hidden. `/etc/gitconfig` and `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config` are now read, though. Any `init.templateDir`, `init.defaultObjectFormat` or `init.defaultRefFormat` set there is written into the fixture repo, and later `GIT_ENV` calls cannot undo it. For example, `src/cli/index.test.ts:297-300` runs `commit` and `checkout` under `GIT_ENV`, with no `hooksPath` pin, so hooks copied in from a template would run. CI runners have no such config, so this would only break on developer machines.

Passing `GIT_ENV` as `opts.env` still routes the call through `runGit`, which is all the decision-73 guard checks, and restores the old behaviour exactly. `opts.env` is applied over the scrubbed env, and `GIT_HISTORY_ENV` still applies last.
